title: MongoDB Connections
summary: Understand documents and collections, then connect Spring Boot to MongoDB.

richText: MongoDB stores documents. A document contains named fields and values.
Field values can include nested documents and arrays.
A collection groups documents. It is separate from other collections in the same database.
BSON is the format MongoDB uses to store documents. It supports values such as dates and ObjectId.
Every document has an _id field that identifies it. ObjectId is one identifier type.
Documents in one collection can have different fields. Validation rules still need to describe what your application accepts.

example.title: A journal entry document
description: This document represents one journal entry. The ID is shown in MongoDB Extended JSON notation.
explanation: title and content are fields in the document.
A collection such as journal_entries stores entries like this one.

richText: Add spring-boot-starter-data-mongodb for blocking MongoDB operations. Let Spring Boot manage its version.
Spring Boot configures the MongoDB client and Spring Data support from the dependency and connection settings.
Use a running local MongoDB server or a managed deployment such as Atlas.
Atlas requires a database user and permitted network access.

example.title: Configure the MongoDB connection
description: Use Spring Boot 3 and Java 17 or later for these examples.
Set MONGODB_URI in the application environment. Include the target database in the URI.
explanation: Spring reads the connection URI from MONGODB_URI.
Keep credentials out of committed configuration files.
If the connection fails, check the URI, credentials, server availability and permitted network access.
